steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "rich/segment.py", "content": "    def split_and_crop_lines(
        cls,
        segments: Iterable["Segment"],
        length: int,
        style: Optional[Style] = None,
        pad: bool = True,
        include_new_lines: bool = True,
    ) -> Iterable[List["Segment"]]:
        """Split segments in to lines, and crop lines greater than a given length.

        Args:
            segments (Iterable[Segment]): An iterable of segments, probably
                generated from console.render.
            length (int): Desired line length.
            style (Style, optional): Style to use for any padding.
            pad (bool): Enable padding of lines that are less than `length`.

        Returns:
            Iterable[List[Segment]]: An iterable of lines of segments.
        """
        line: List[Segment] = []
        append = line.append

        adjust_line_length = cls.adjust_line_length
        new_line_segment = cls("\n")

        for segment in segments:
            if "\n" in segment.text and not segment.control:
                text, segment_style, _ = segment
                while text:
                    _text, new_line, text = text.partition("\n")
                    if _text:
                        append(cls(_text, segment_style))
                    if new_line:
                        cropped_line = adjust_line_length(
                            line, length, style=style, pad=pad
                        )
                        if include_new_lines:
                            cropped_line.append(new_line_segment)
                        yield cropped_line
                        line.clear()
            else:
                append(segment)
        if line:
            yield adjust_line_length(line, length, style=style, pad=pad)

    def adjust_line_length(

            pad (bool, optional): Pad lines with spaces if they are shorter than `length`. Defaults to True.

        Returns:
            List[Segment]: A line of segments with the desired length.
        """
        line_length = sum(segment.cell_length for segment in line)
        new_line: List[Segment]

        if line_length < length:
            if pad:

{"status": "ok", "filepath": "rich/console.py", "content": "    def _render_buffer(self, buffer: Iterable[Segment]) -> str:
        """Render buffered output, and clear buffer."""
        output: List[str] = []
        append = output.append
        color_system = self._color_system
        legacy_windows = self.legacy_windows
        not_terminal = not self.is_terminal
        if self.no_color and color_system:
            buffer = Segment.remove_color(buffer)
        for text, style, control in buffer:
            if style:
                append(
                    style.render(
                        text,
                        color_system=color_system,
                        legacy_windows=legacy_windows,
                    )
                )
            elif not (not_terminal and control):
                append(text)

        rendered = "".join(output)
        return rendered

    def input(
        self,
        prompt: TextType = "",
        *,
        markup: bool = True,
        emoji: bool = True,
        password: bool = False,
        stream: Optional[TextIO] = None,
    ) -> str:
        """Displays a prompt and waits for input from the user. The prompt may contain color / style.

        It works in the same way as Python's builtin :func:`input` function and provides elaborate line editing and history features if Python's builtin :mod:`readline` module is previously loaded.

        Args:
            prompt (Union[str, Text]): Text to render in the prompt.
            markup (bool, optional): Enable console markup (requires a str prompt). Defaults to True.
            emoji (bool, optional): Enable emoji (requires a str prompt). Defaults to True.
            password: (bool, optional): Hide typed text. Defaults to False.
            stream: (TextIO, optional): Optional file to read input from (rather than stdin). Defaults to None.

        Returns:
            str: Text read from stdin.
        """
        if prompt:
            self.print(prompt, markup=markup, emoji=emoji, end="")
        if password:
            result = getpass("", stream=stream)
        else:
            if stream:
                result = stream.readline()
            else:
                result = input()
        return result

    def export_text(self, *, clear: bool = True, styles: bool = False) -> str:
        """Generate text from console contents (requires record=True argument in constructor).

        Args:
            clear (bool, optional): Clear record buffer after exporting. Defaults to ``True``.
            styles (bool, optional): If ``True``, ansi escape codes will be included. ``False`` for plain text.
                Defaults to ``False``.

        Returns:
            str: String containing console contents.

        """
        assert (
            self.record
        ), "To export console contents set record=True in the constructor or instance"

        with self._record_buffer_lock:
            if styles:
                text = "".join(
                    (style.render(text) if style else text)
                    for text, style, _ in self._record_buffer
                )
            else:
                text = "".join(
                    segment.text
                    for segment in self._record_buffer
                    if not segment.control
                )
            if clear:
                del self._record_buffer[:]
        return text
